title: Safe People, Trusted Adults & Asking for Help (Child Track)
description: Guides children to identify trusted adults at home, school, and in the community, and practise simple ways to ask for help whenever they feel worried or unsafe.

sections.title: Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Safe People, Trusted Adults & Asking for Help (Child Track)

content.title: Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Safe People, Trusted Adults & Asking for Help (Child Track)
content.overview: This section provides a trauma-informed, practical guide to understanding the core purpose of safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) and how it shapes physical, emotional, and relational safety in daily family life. Designed for children identifying their Safety Hand of 5 trusted adults and how to ask for help (SS-CHD-007/008), it focuses on realistic, repeatable steps that strengthen safety, predictability, and connection.
content.psychoeducation: Why does safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) matter in section 1? Children and families thrive on predictability, nervous-system safety, and attuned repair. When safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) is practised consistently, stress responses decrease and relational trust grows. By focusing on understanding the core purpose of safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) and how it shapes physical, emotional, and relational safety in daily family life, caregivers and practitioners create a calmer, safer environment where children can regulate and develop confidence.
learning_goals: Define what safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) means in your own words before and after learning.
Recognise how safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) supports child safety, emotional wellbeing, and nervous-system regulation.
Practise simple, non-defensive scripts and responses for safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) during everyday moments.
Identify early warning signs, barriers, and support pathways related to safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
step_by_step: Pause & Ground: Notice your own breathing, body tension, and tone before addressing safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
Observe Factually: Notice what is happening in the moment around safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) without blame or judgement.
Connect & Validate: Acknowledge feelings and safety needs clearly and calmly.
Respond Simply: Choose one clear, age-appropriate action or boundary for safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
Reflect & Repair: Review what worked, repair any rupture honestly, and record your next small step.
parent_scripts: "I can see this moment feels big right now. Let's slow down and take one step together with safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track)."
"Everyone is safe here. We can talk about what happened and work out the next step calmly."
"I noticed I was getting stressed. I'm taking a breath so I can listen properly."
"We don't have to get everything perfect today — we are practising safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) one routine at a time."
practical_examples: Everyday Routine: Applying safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) during a busy morning or bedtime transition by slowing down, offering two calm choices, and keeping tone steady.
Moment of Stress: When tension rises around safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track), pausing for 10 seconds before speaking, validating feelings, and focusing on safety first.

Follow-Through & Review: Recording a factual note after practising safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) to notice what helped the child settle and what support would help next time.

content_variants.toddlers: For babies & toddlers (0–4): Focus on gentle tone, physical comfort, predictable routines, and simple 3-to-5 word reassurance while practising safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
content_variants.school_age: For school-age children (5–11): Use clear explanations, visual routines, curiosity about their feelings, and collaborative problem-solving around safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
content_variants.teens: For adolescents (12–18): Respect autonomy, listen without lecturing, agree on clear safety boundaries, and involve teens in decisions about safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
content_variants.fatherhood: For fathers & male caregivers: Model calm accountability, steady emotional presence, and non-frightening leadership when practising safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).

red_flags: Immediate physical danger, threats, intimidation, or coercive control observed during safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
A child shows fear, freezing, dissociation, or disclosure of harm related to safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
An adult is unable to regulate or maintain safe supervision while attempting safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track).
Signs of acute mental health crisis or substance intoxication affecting child safety.
when_to_escalate: Pause learning immediately if anyone is in danger and use verified emergency or crisis supports.
Follow jurisdiction-specific child protection and mandatory reporting obligations when harm is disclosed or suspected.
Engage a qualified supervisor, specialist DFV practitioner, or clinician when risk exceeds self-directed learning.

trauma_informed.relational: Attachment lens for safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track): Prioritises connection before correction, attunement to cues, shame-free accountability, and timely repair after ruptures.
trauma_informed.justice: Fairness & cultural lens for safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track): Respects cultural strengths, kinship networks, neurodiversity, disability access, and structural barriers without equating poverty with neglect.

sections.simplified_parent_version:
What safe people, trusted adults & asking for help (child track) means:
Safe People, Trusted Adults & Asking for Help (Child Track) is about keeping daily life safe, calm, and predictable so your child feels supported and understood.

How to practise it:
1. Pause and take one slow breath first.
2. Notice what your child needs right now.
3. Use a calm voice and one clear step.
4. Repair kindly if things go off track.
